title: Single-pair shortest path: simple-path enumeration vs Dijkstra
problem_statement: Given a directed graph with non-negative edge weights and vertices s, t, compute the minimum total weight of an s-t path. The harness uses complete digraphs given as n x n weight matrices, s = 0, t = n - 1.

algorithms.name: simple-path enumeration
algorithms.idea: Depth-first search over every simple path from s, recording the cheapest one that reaches t.
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(n (n-2)!) on the complete digraph (~ e (n-2)! simple s-t paths, n neighbour checks per search node)
algorithms.correctness: With non-negative weights some shortest walk is a simple path, and all simple paths are enumerated.

algorithms.name: Dijkstra (array version)
algorithms.idea: Repeatedly settle the unsettled vertex with the smallest tentative distance and relax its out-edges.
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(n^2) with an array (linear in the n x n weight-matrix input; it reads exactly n(n-1)/2 distinct weights, for each pair of vertices the one leaving the vertex settled first), which is optimal up to a constant factor for weight-matrix input: for n >= 4 split the n - 2 vertices other than s, t into U (floor((n-2)/2) of them) and W, and set w(s, u) = 1, w(u, x) = 2 and w(x, t) = 1 for u in U, x in W, all other weights 100; then dist(s, t) = 4, and lowering any one weight w(u, x) to 1 makes it 3, so on this instance every correct deterministic algorithm (and every run of a zero-error randomized one) reads all floor((n-2)^2/4) weights w(u, x). O(m + n log n) with Fibonacci heaps
algorithms.correctness: Dijkstra 1959: with non-negative weights, the minimum tentative distance is final when a vertex is settled.

relationship: Enumeration is factorial (super-exponential) on dense graphs; Dijkstra's greedy settling order yields Theta(n^2).

sources.title: A note on two problems in connexion with graphs

sources.authors: Fredman, M. L.; Tarjan, R. E.
sources.title: Fibonacci heaps and their uses in improved network optimization algorithms

sources.authors: Duan, R.; Mao, J.; Mao, X.; Shu, X.; Yin, L.
sources.title: Breaking the Sorting Barrier for Directed Single-Source Shortest Paths
sources.note: O(m log^(2/3) n) deterministic SSSP, beating Dijkstra on sparse graphs.

verification.method: V1: both agree on random complete digraphs with weights in [1, 100] (n <= 8 for enumeration). V2: runtimes fitted against n (n-2)! and n^2.

caveats: Enumeration cost is graph-dependent; the factorial bound is for complete graphs. Negative weights would require Bellman-Ford (O(nm)).
notes: Further T3 entries: array Dijkstra Theta(n^2) -> Fibonacci-heap Dijkstra O(m + n log n) -> Duan et al. 2025 O(m log^(2/3) n) on sparse graphs.
